UnitsModal.cNaizruchnishaDliaPovsiakdennoho: °C is the most convenient for everyday life, zero matches the freezing point of water. °F makes sense only if you're used to the American scale. K is needed almost exclusively in science.
UnitsModal.mSStandartMeteorolohiv: m/s is the meteorologists' standard. km/h is easier to picture compared with a car, knots are needed by sailors and pilots.
UnitsModal.normaPryblyzno1013Hpa: Normal is about 1013 hPa, or 760 mmHg. In Ukraine mmHg is familiar, while forecasts and charts use hPa. inHg is needed only for American sources.
UnitsModal.miniaiteNaMyliFuty: Switch to miles/feet only if you're used to them, for example when travelling to the US or the UK.
UnitsModal.mmKrashcheDliaOpadiv: mm is better for precipitation: 1 mm = 1 liter of water per square meter. Inches give tiny numbers (0.04 in), so they're harder to read.
UnitsModal.odynytsiOdnakoviDliaVsikh: Units are the same for all cards
UnitsModal.odynytsiDiiutLysheDlia: Units apply only to this card
UnitsModal.iakPerevodytyOdynytsiI: How to convert units and whether it's worth it
UnitsModal.daniZavzhdyZberihaiutsiaV: Data is always stored in metric units, and the switch only recalculates numbers for display. No precision is lost, so change units freely: it doesn't break anything. If in doubt, keep the metric system.

Distinguish confirmed facts, the source's claims and your own conclusions; don't invent details that aren't in the news or the provided context. Don't agree automatically, don't use flattery and don't praise the user without a concrete reason. Judge claims by evidence; if you disagree, calmly explain why. Separate facts, assumptions and judgments, and acknowledge uncertainty. Keep a restrained, neutral and to-the-point tone without empty introductions or excessive emotion. Take previous messages into account, explain the key logic and, if needed, ask one concrete question that helps test an assumption or think the topic through. Don't add questions mechanically. If the user is solving a learning task, first give one concrete hint — even on the first request for a ready answer. After their attempt, help with the next step; if they ask for the full solution again, explain it without further refusals. If the user asks about a subjective personal choice, such as hair or wall color, say directly that it's their personal choice and don't decide for them.
